name: Mississippi Civil Rights Museum
unique: A state museum that tells the movement county by county, with the names of the dead, a burned church bell and the story of Freedom Summer.
buzz: One of the best civil rights museums in the country, and the scale of the local detail is what makes it. Pair it with the adjacent history museum.

name: Mississippi Museum of Art
unique: A state art museum with a strong collection of Mississippi and Southern artists, photography and a sculpture garden.
buzz: The Southern art is the reason, and the museum is quiet and well organized. Free on some days.

name: Fondren
unique: A walkable neighborhood of bungalows, coffee shops, bars, a brewery and a cinema, the social center of young Jackson.
buzz: The district is compact and busy on weekends, with a good brunch scene. Park once and walk.

name: Longwood
unique: The largest octagonal house in the country, unfinished since the Civil War, with its original crates and tools still inside.
buzz: The unfinished interior is the fascinating part, and the tour explains why construction stopped. Book ahead in pilgrimage season.

name: Melrose
unique: A Greek Revival mansion in the Natchez National Historical Park, with original furniture and the story of the enslaved people who ran the estate.
buzz: The ranger tours are excellent and the slave quarters exhibit is part of the visit. Less flashy than the private houses and more honest.

name: Old Court House Museum
unique: A 1858 courthouse on a hill with a museum of the siege, Confederate and Union relics, and a view over the Mississippi.
buzz: The collection is old fashioned and dense, and the view from the hill is the best in town. Pair it with the military park.

name: Oxford Square
unique: A courthouse square of bookshops, bars, boutiques and restaurants, with the university a few blocks away and game day crowds that fill it.
buzz: The square is the town's living room, busy on weekends and game days. The independent bookstore is the local anchor.

name: Rowan Oak
unique: William Faulkner's home, preserved with his books, his outline of A Fable on the wall and the grounds he walked.
buzz: Pilgrimage for readers, and the self guided tour lets you linger. The cedar grove is quiet.

name: Delta Blues Museum
unique: A museum in a former railroad depot with Muddy Waters' cabin, guitars, photographs and the story of the Delta blues.
buzz: The cabin and the instruments are the highlights, and Clarksdale itself is the experience. Go to a juke joint after.

name: GRAMMY Museum Mississippi
unique: A museum of recorded music with instruments, stage clothes and interactive mixing stations, focused on Mississippi's outsize role in American music.
buzz: The interactive studios are fun for kids and the artifacts are serious. A surprise for a small Delta town.

name: Dentzel Carousel
unique: A 1909 Dentzel menagerie carousel with hand carved animals, still running in a pavilion in Highland Park.
buzz: The animals are beautiful and the ride costs a dollar. A genuine piece of Americana.

name: African American Military History Museum
unique: A museum in a 1942 USO building telling the stories of Black soldiers from the Revolution to today, with uniforms, medals and oral histories.
buzz: Personal and well curated, and free. The local soldiers' stories are the strongest part.

name: Beauvoir
unique: Jefferson Davis's last home and presidential library, with the house, the Confederate cemetery and the grounds on the Gulf.
buzz: The house and the library are the visit, and the view of the Gulf is a bonus. The history is presented uncritically, so bring your own context.

name: Biloxi Lighthouse
unique: A 1848 lighthouse standing in the middle of a highway, with a climb to the top and a view of the beach and the bay.
buzz: The setting in the median is strange and the climb is short. A quick photo stop.

name: Shearwater Pottery
unique: A family pottery studio founded by the Anderson family, with a showroom of glazed pots and tiles made on site.
buzz: The pottery is beautiful and the prices are fair for handmade work. Pair it with the Walter Anderson Museum.

name: Tennessee Williams Home
unique: The boyhood home of the playwright, with family furniture, photographs and the bedroom where he wrote his first stories.
buzz: Small and personal, best for theater people. The Columbus historic district around it is worth a walk.

name: Cotton District
unique: A neighborhood of restored mill cottages, bars and restaurants next to the Mississippi State campus, rebuilt after a tornado.
buzz: The district is walkable and busy on game weekends. Good for a casual dinner.

name: Natchez Trace Visitor Center
unique: The headquarters of the Natchez Trace Parkway, with a museum on the old trace, a film and the start of the 444 mile drive.
buzz: The film and the exhibits explain why the trace exists, and the parkway is the real attraction. Free.
